fatal_blockers: Proposal 1 does not specify the block lattice, target, normalized search class for Q, retraction map, or inequalities covering DROP, G13, and G19 states. Because Q is variable, the eigenvalue-bounded shell is circular, rationalization requires certified strict margins, and an eight-clause pass cannot establish G20–G22 scaling.

Proposal 2 relies on quadratic Plücker relations although CVP residuals are linear; selector linearization reopens independent signed charts, G13 affine lifts, and G19-style trades. Salts, transitions, target, baseline, coefficient bound, and the claimed D/W recurrence are not frozen, so the proposed enumeration is not executable or asymptotically discriminating.

Proposal 3 does not defeat G19: noncommutative multiplication tables become linear flow constraints after selectors are emitted and remain vulnerable to signed splicing. An A5 test cannot examine a growing PSL2 family, uniform displacement, or whether the baseline from full table selectors overwhelms the claimed Ω(sqrt(p)) penalty.

Proposal 4's CRT shell injectivity does not exclude exact zero-residual integral trades in the fully emitted linear digit-and-carry system; it must explicitly defeat the G13 affine lift and G19 splicing. The completeness cost of anchored carries and the dependence of the coefficient shell on M are unaccounted for, and no concrete equations or target are supplied.

Proposal 5 still fails the Generation-27 reopening condition: the base target, glue map, port equivalence, matched control, and legal/illegal contracted costs are not frozen. Enumerating only through B+32 can omit expensive boundary states that later re-enter cheaply, while ordinary min-plus powers give additive cycle-mean growth rather than the asserted exponential ratio absent an explicit recursive inequality.

Proposal 6's degree-three experiment on the constant eight-clause formula cannot discriminate the central exponential-degree, rank, or coefficient-height obstruction for general formulas. Kronecker compression has no proved Euclidean separation, and the proposed dual-functional coordinate lacks a uniformly constructible definition and bounded norm.

Proposal 7 turns nonlinear tables into linear selector constraints, so short integral trades and signed pseudocodewords remain the decisive G7/G13/G19 obstruction. No specific expander, quasigroup tables, lattice target, baseline, or spectral coefficient bound is frozen, and a length-12 pass would not test uniform integral expansion.
evidence: G13 verifies an exact coefficient-sum-one affine collision, and G15 lifts it through every tested hierarchy node with zero residual below threshold. This directly blocks claims that enlarged linear encodings automatically remove affine pseudodistributions.
G19 verifies an exact accepting signed flow with two negative coefficients and zero residual. Nonlinearity before selector emission did not survive unrestricted integral CVP coefficients.

G7, G9, and G11 exhibit constant-cost zero-residual signed kernels, while G12 shows that charging one such kernel exposes a cheaper DROP state. Residual scaling alone therefore supplies no polynomial relative gap.
G14 is only a finite B+32 pair-bag shell pass. The supplied Generation-27 gate explicitly rejected truncated recursive-state searches without complete ports, glue, closure, and a noncircular bound.
No Generation-28 proposal supplies verifier output or a fully specified emitted lattice, so none of its expected moves is experimental evidence.
